verdicts.reason: Quotes verified verbatim. 09.01.02:56 INV-6 names the work-for-hire contributor as a valid, unpruned 0% row, :188 renders that row as '0% — paid by fee, not by share', and :260 asserts 'A 0% row that says "paid by fee" is the difference between a contributor who was paid and a contributor who was forgotten.' 09.02.03:48/:70 state the extinguishment party is 'absent from the ledger by agreement', DT-01 at :176 rejects the bare 0% row and resolves to 'present in the view, structurally distinct in the record', D-02 at :213 makes '0% by agreement' structurally distinct, 09.02.04 D-14 at :277 forbids an amendment producing a 0% row, and 09.02-split-capture-agreements-cx.md:10 CX-01 says designation 'removes them from the ledger'. That is a real, unmarked representational contradiction — 09.01.02:260 says the annotated 0% row IS the distinction, 09.02.03 DT-01 says a 0% row cannot be it. DOWNGRADED from blocking because every consequence the finding says is undecided is in fact decided at D-level elsewhere: 09.02.01 D-09 at :252 settles visibility ('fee parties see its shape, not its percentages') and consenter status ('A bought-out drummer is not a ledger party'), 09.02.03:115 settles the capture-view rendering ('Fee, no share — consented, £200'), and rights-ownership-cx.md:216 settles notification fan-out ('notifies the performer even when their ledger share is 0% or fee-only'). The forcedInvention claim that INV-6 is left with no population is also refuted — 09.01.05:37 keeps the non-featured performer, and 09.01.02:257 already concedes 'a session drummer is a 0% ledger row (or absent entirely)'. What survives is a schema-level divergence and stale wording in 09.01.02, not an undecided product behaviour.

Quotes verified (09.01.01:91, :363, D-07 at :390; 09.01.02:35, :152; 09.01.02's Cross-Cut Note at :253 indeed never mentions lineage). But the substance is answered by a ratified decision, not left open: 09.01.01 D-07 at :390 states the complete rule — 'edit-of, remaster-of, alternate-take-of inherit the parent's consented master ledger by reference; kinds that add one (remix-of, re-recording-of) do not', with ':91 Inheritance is by reference, not by copy … until someone forks it, at which point it becomes an independent ledger requiring its own consent' and ':93 The default is presented and overridable in both directions'. 09.01.02 states no competing rule — a full-tree scan for 'inherit|by reference|edit-of' returns no lineage statement anywhere outside 09.01.01, so there is no second normative position for an implementer to pick. 09.01.02:35 defines a ledger's attachment and :152 describes a capture-created object; by-reference sharing leaves the ledger attached to the parent and is not contradicted by either. 09.01.01:363 is a coordination note ('must be reconciled at Step 6') that states its own position and defers only the propagation of that decision into a sibling file — a documentation gap, not a divergence in product behaviour.

Quotes verified verbatim. rights-ownership-cx.md:238 — 'A term-limited buyout additionally schedules a future reversion event (async, notify-not-execute)' — stands head-on against 09.03.02 D-02 at :99 — 'Conditional reversion: notify, never auto-execute. Fixed-term reversion: auto-execute' — and against :35 'Term expiry produces a reversion event with no actor — the passage of time writes to the chain' plus D-04 at :101 (atomic chain+registry write). 09.02.03:130 verified and takes the notify side, though its qualifier 'on a conditional reversion' mislabels a fixed-term expiry. A term-limited buyout's expiry is a date passing, so both statements cannot hold. DOWNGRADED from blocking because the shared authority both sides cite resolves it determinately in one direction: rights-ownership-index.md:116 D-05 reads 'Arithmetic (a date passing) executes; interpretation notifies', and 09.03.02 D-02 restates exactly that for this case. No product behaviour has to be invented — the CX-09 line and 09.02.03:130 need correcting against D-05.

All quotes verified. But the two value sets are attributes of different objects at different granularity, and the tree resolves which one the public badge renders. 09.03.01 D-01 at :100 scopes its enum to events — 'Every event carries a trust level: platform-witnessed / evidence-attached / asserted'. 09.01.03:193 scopes the other to records — 'A master ledger carries a provenance class', with captured/asserted/imported at :197-199. The badge question is explicitly closed: 09.01.03 Q-08 at :335 is struck through and marked 'RESOLVED — registry-wide', citing rights-ownership-cx.md CX-07 that 'Every rendered record carries its provenance class (captured / asserted / imported)' and stating 'the chain owns the provenance facts; the lookup owns the derived badge, which cannot be set independently of the chain'. rights-ownership-cx.md:25/:180-184 say the same. The lookup's badge value set is therefore captured/asserted/imported, derived from chain facts; 09.06.04:50 and DT-03 at :92 say 'the same attribute' and 'inherited from' as loose provenance-of-the-idea phrasing, not as an assertion that the per-event enum is the per-record enum. No forced invention: 'evidence-attached' has no record-level counterpart because it is an event-level qualifier, and 'imported' has no event-level counterpart because it describes a record's source.

Quotes verified verbatim at 09.01.03:159 ('Every block is overridable by an owner with an attested reason, recorded as a chain event and notified to the encumbrance holder') and D-06 at :316 ('Every block is overridable by an owner, attested, recorded, and notified to the holder'). The governed table at :145-157 contains rows whose blocker is not an encumbrance and has no holder to notify: :147 'unallocated or disputed ledger', :148 and :153 'The deterministic recorded master-action consent evaluator'. The same file then states those blocks as absolute: :231 'Minority owner (10%) adds an encumbrance to sabotage a release | Blocked under the default rule' and :266 'Control Summary blocks every exploitation action naming the dispute'. Read literally, D-06 hands the 10% owner the exact override :231 forecloses. The rationale at :160-162 is scoped to stale platform bookkeeping about external facts, which does not reach the owners' own recorded consent rule — but that scoping is nowhere stated as a limit on D-06. Q-06 at :333 asks only whether notification is the holder's entire remedy, which presupposes a holder exists and does not close this. Warning is the right level: the divergence is bounded to which table rows the override reaches.

Quotes verified verbatim and the arithmetic checks out. 09.01.04 D-05 at :250 states the anchoring invariant '∀W: Σ(publisher rows anchored to W) = writer_share(W)'; a writer with an undeclared publishing position has zero anchored rows, so the invariant fails. 09.01.04:162 states the consequence of that failure as 'the ledger stays unallocated and Propose is disabled', and 09.01.02:163 confirms 'When the pools satisfy INV-1..INV-7, the Propose action unlocks'. Yet the same file's States table at :196 says undeclared positions leave the ledger where it 'cannot leave proposed', and :182 says an off-platform writer's ledger 'stays proposed' with a chase running ('Waiting on 1 of 3'). :159 does not rescue it — the auto-created self-held row applies to a writer who declares they have no publisher, while :182 insists an undeclared position is 'never rendered as self-published'. The two states differ materially: unallocated blocks release, licence and payout (09.01.02:134) and no consent has been solicited; proposed means rows are pending and the chase has begun.

Quotes verified verbatim. rights-ownership-cx.md:21 CX-03 and :91 assert 'disputed freezes payouts and blocks every exploitation verdict', and 09.01.03 ships it as built behaviour: :147 lists 'disputed ledger' as a Blocked-by for 'Release / distribute', :148 for granting a non-exclusive master licence, :149 for an exclusive one, and :266 'Control Summary blocks every exploitation action naming the dispute'. Simultaneously 09.04.03 Q-04 at :112 and 09.04 index Q-02 at :61 carry the identical question as an unresolved [OWNER] values trade queued to /create-prd, and Q-04 is explicit that only the pre-delivery half is settled ('domain 12 makes a frozen recording ineligible pre-delivery … but the live-release and licensing halves are an unresolved values trade'). This is not a well-formed deferral being flagged: the deferral is well-formed, and other files contradict it as though it were closed. 09.01.03:148 blocking a non-exclusive licence is precisely the licensing half Q-04 says is open.

Quotes verified, but the owning mechanism resolves it and the 'pro rata' lines are summaries of the offered default, not a competing automatic rule. 09.02.04:142-144 reads 'Pro rata is offered as the neutral transform because it is the only one that preserves the parties' own agreed proportions … it is never a silent default and never the only option' — so pro rata IS the presented transform in the owning file too. Routing is explicit and one-directional: 09.01.06:39-42 says an interpolation 'mutates the ledger (see CX-02) … which requires their re-consent (09.02.04)', :54 says 'the ledger dilution is proposed and re-consented', 09.01.02:255 says 'The declaration must never write shares directly', and 09.01.01:364 instructs 'This file must not re-implement dilution + re-consent'. An implementer therefore reaches 09.02.04's machinery, where the proposer picks the basis and 'the record names who chose it'. The CX-02 phrasing at 09.01-rights-registry-cx.md:49 and 09.01.04:178 describes what pro rata does to anchored publisher rows, not an instruction to apply it without a chooser.

Both quotes verified (09.01-rights-registry-cx.md:42; 09.01.02:196). They do not conflict. CX-01 synthesis 5's stated concern is 'a ledger that totals correctly but that neither agreed to' — i.e. a binding ledger produced without consent. The carve-out is scoped to exactly the window where nothing is binding: 'within unallocated only — nobody has consented, so there is nothing to protect', with 'every change attributed in a visible edit trail' and 'At Propose, the whole ledger plus its trail is what parties review'. The consent-binding write is still a proposal requiring whole-ledger consent (09.01.02 D-01 at :276, D-06 at :281, D-09 at :284), so the CX rule holds unbroken. The two citing files apply the rule to different objects and reach the strict answer there: 09.01.01 D-12 at :395 rejects concurrent link writes outright, and 09.01.04:184 requires a rebase-and-re-present on a transfer/amendment race. No reasonable implementer builds last-write-wins on a consented ledger from this text.

The quote at 09.01.03:154 is verbatim, but the row is not undecidable. It names a concrete blocker — 'An exclusive grant's delivery obligations' — which is exactly what the three-verdict evaluator consumes: blocker present → Blocked; absent → No recorded obstacle; source unreachable → Unknown (D-05 at :315, and the degradation rule at :139-141 and :264). Both implementers emit the same verdict from the same input, so nothing is invented. The trailing clause 'separate takedown governance remains unresolved' is a scope disclaimer of the same kind as :91-94, which lists 'takedown governance' alongside release consent and payout calculation as things the master-action consent rule deliberately does not answer — and takedown of a live release sits with domain 12 (09.03.02:62 escalates it there, 09.03.02 Q-03 at :109 tracks the auto-vs-notify posture to /create-prd-security, naming 12.05.03 Q-01 as its sibling). The finding's premise that one row of the table cannot emit a verdict is not supported by the row's own text.

Quotes verified, but the operative predicate is consent-completeness, not time, and the file supplies it. 09.01.03 Happy Path 8 at :210 sets the value from the consent event alone — 'Every named party consents to the whole master ledger plus its encumbrance list. Provenance class is set to captured' — with no time test anywhere in the flow. The sibling values partition on the same axis: :198 defines asserted as 'Entered retroactively by one party; no counterparty consented', and :199 defines imported by source ('Ingested from a DSP, distributor or CMS feed'). The finding's 'late but unanimous' case therefore lands cleanly: counterparties did consent, so it is not asserted; it was not ingested from a feed, so it is not imported; Happy Path 8 makes it captured. 'At or near creation, in the room' at :197 is the descriptive gloss on the wedge, and DT-08 at :279 confirms the intended cut is one-party-self-assertion versus multi-party consent, not early versus late. No time window is needed and none is implied by any rule.

Quotes verified, but the 'one mechanism' evidence is misapplied and the two cadences are not asserted to be the same schedule. 09.02.01:229 reads 'Capture's edit-invalidates-consent rule (D-07) is the same mechanism as amendment's re-consent, applied pre-lock' — that is the consent-invalidation rule, not the notification cadence. Each feature states its own requirement on the shared cross-cut: 09.02.01:108 says 'This feature's requirement on the Consent Chase & Escalating Notification cross-cut' before its table at :112-118, and rights-ownership-cx.md:289 records those as 'Requirements this domain imposes'. 09.02.04:172 specifies amendment's own cadence. Crucially the two non-negotiable rules survive in both: no expiry (09.02.01:109 'The sheet never expires'; 09.02.04:172 'The proposal never expires and silence is never converted into consent') and never-deemed-consent (09.02.04:221 'Never resolves itself into consent'). The day-45 'blocked' badge is a proposal state, not an expiry, so it does not breach the no-expiry requirement. Different features imposing different reminder cadences on a shared notifier is not a contradiction.

The States row at 09.04.02:71 is quoted verbatim, but the substantive question it touches is a well-formed tracked deferral and the governing rule is stated. 09.04.02 Q-01 at :104 is '[OWNER] How does a dispute end when both parties dig in?' with owner User and target /create-prd, duplicated at 09.04 index Q-01 at :60, 09.04.03 Q-01 at :109 and domain Q-07 — that is the deadline-with-consequence question, tracked with an owner and a target. The behavioural rule meanwhile is unambiguous at 09.04.02:57: 'The share stays frozen until one party withdraws, a court judgment is recorded, or an agreed end-mechanism is chosen', with the termination mechanism explicitly badged '[PENDING — resolution of Q-01 at /create-prd]'. The finding's premise that any deadline must carry an adjudicative consequence is also wrong — a response deadline that simply flips the copy from 'Awaiting X's position' to 'no response received' changes no share and no payment, and so does not touch 09.04.03 DT-03's adjudication-by-timeout concern at :85. The remaining gap is the numeric value, which 09.04.02 Q-03 at :106 itself characterises as downstream tuning.

Every quote verified verbatim. 09.01.06:16 claims ownership of the status flag and enumerates it as 'cleared / uncleared / pending'. The file then never uses two of those three: :52 resolves to 'cleared-by-licence', :53 sets 'uncleared', :54 says 'on success the status flips' without naming the target value, :62 introduces 'source-unknown', and :64 re-uses 'cleared-by-licence' with a scope qualifier. 'pending' never reappears and bare 'cleared' never appears as a value. The States table at :71-77 is confirmed to enumerate render states (Loading / Empty / Populated / Partial / Error), not status values, so it supplies no enum either. The unresolved case is concrete and consequential: clearance obtained by negotiation through domain 11 (:54) has no named status, while both 'uncleared' (:61) and 'source-unknown' (:62) are stated to be release-blocking and so cannot be distinguished by effect. Two implementers will build different enums with different release-gate predicates.

Quotes verified verbatim, and the tracking is malformed rather than valid. 09.05.03:70 carries a bare '[PENDING] — CX-04, low confidence, unresolved' with no owner and no stage. Its only target is 09.05-ai-voice-likeness-consent-cx.md:69, 'CX-03 and CX-04 synthesis questions are deferred to /ideate-discover Step 5, per the CX gate' — a stage that has run, since the tree carries completed Step-6 CX syntheses (rights-ownership-cx.md:46, :222). CX-04 itself at :13 is marked Low confidence and 'its handling is unresolved'. Confirmed that no open question absorbs it: 09.05.03's Q list and the 09.05 index contain nothing on the recursive case. The same expired-stage, no-owner pattern recurs at 09.05-ai-voice-likeness-consent-cx.md:67 for a NIL grant withdrawn after release. The forced choice is real — whether a training-consent position is grantable over a work carrying a declared AI-generated element, when 09.05.01 D-01 anchors grants to parties who demonstrably hold the right and 09.05.03 treats AI-generated material as possibly unprotectable — with no tracked question to escalate to. Warning rather than blocking because it is an edge case at the boundary of two features, not a mainline flow.

Quotes verified, but the operative statements converge on the recording's owners and the parenthetical is a loose cross-reference, not a competing definition. 09.06.01:52-53 states the rule subject explicitly — 'When two ISRCs are found on one recording … lets the recording's owners decide' — and D-05 at :124 restates it without any gloss: 'the owners confirm the canonical code'. The scope row at :36 pins ISRC to 'One recording', and :43 reinforces that a radio edit is a distinct recording needing its own code. The parenthetical '(the rights holders on the work per [09.01.01])' points at the file that owns both object types and their links (09.01.01:20 'This feature owns the objects and the links between them'); read against three surrounding statements naming the recording, no competent implementer resolves it to the writer/publisher pool of 09.01.04. This is imprecise wording worth fixing, not a party-set divergence.

Quoted verbatim and the off-by-one is real. 09.01.01:308 pairs the scenario 'Live set recorded as one continuous file containing 12 songs … the system suggests the better shape first' with the trigger 'Above 12 linked works'. A 12-work medley is not above 12, so the row's own worked example falls outside its own stated trigger and the promised suggestion never fires. Checked the surrounding medley rows (:303-307) and D-05 at :388 — no other threshold statement exists anywhere in the file to disambiguate, so the boundary is decided by whichever reading an implementer picks. Warning, not blocking: the suggestion is explicitly 'Suggestion only — never forced', so the divergence changes a nudge string at exactly one input value and carries no rights or money consequence.
